original.excerpt: Group averaging maps every feasible top-singular-space balance weight to an invariant feasible weight, and every invariant positive-semidefinite weight on a real isotypic component is represented by Hermitian positive-semidefinite multiplicity blocks over the division algebras R, C, and H.
original.context: The model clarification preserves this previous shorthand claim. Its referenced proof uses row/column permutations; the sentence alone omits that hypothesis.

witness.explanation: Constant-diagonal feasibility is preserved by permutations, not by arbitrary orthogonal conjugation. Whether this is an actual scope error depends on which inherited assumptions governed the shorthand node.
witness.evidence: Set A=U=V=I_2, H=[[1,1/2],[1/2,1]], and R=(1/sqrt(2))*[[1,1],[1,-1]]. Then R^2=I and RA=AR, while RHR^T=diag(3/2,1/2). The group average (H+RHR^T)/2 has diagonal (5/4,3/4), not (1,1). This refutes an arbitrary-orthogonal-action extension, but does not refute the explicitly permutation-scoped source proof.
